Definition: from a compound of G1537 and the base of G939 (meaning to go out); an exit (literally or figuratively):--end, way to escape.
BiblicalUsage: This word is an exit, a way out, and by extension the end of a life, and it occurs twice. Paul promises that God will make a way to escape every temptation, so that we may be able to bear it, and Hebrews tells us to consider the end of our leaders' lives and follow their faith. The word holds both the door out of trouble and the end of the road.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God always makes a way out, because He never allows a temptation without also providing the escape.
